title: IBRANCE (palbociclib) Dose-Action Triage
instruction: For each clinical finding, sort it into the action that the current IBRANCE prescribing information actually requires: continue the existing dose, or hold and adjust it.

items.prompt: Absolute neutrophil count of 900 cells/mm3 on Day 1 of a new cycle, patient afebrile
items.rationale: An ANC of 900 cells/mm3 falls in the label's Grade 3 band. The dose-modification table specifies that Grade 3 (or recurrent Grade 3) neutropenia found on Day 1 of a cycle must be withheld until recovery to Grade ≤2 and then resumed at the next lower dose; fever is not required to trigger this.

items.prompt: Absolute neutrophil count of 300 cells/mm3 on routine labs; patient reports feeling entirely well
items.rationale: An ANC of 300 cells/mm3 is Grade 4 neutropenia. The label recommends dose interruption, reduction, or delay for patients who develop Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia regardless of whether the patient is symptomatic.

items.prompt: New, isolated dry cough without fever, dyspnea, or hypoxia, four weeks into therapy
items.rationale: Labeling directs clinicians to hold IBRANCE and evaluate any new or worsening respiratory symptom suspected to be pneumonitis; dyspnea, hypoxia, or fever are not required for this action to apply.

citations.title: Ibrance (palbociclib) dosing, indications, interactions, adverse effects, and more - Medscape

items.prompt: Severe renal impairment with creatinine clearance of 20 mL/min identified before starting therapy
items.rationale: The label states no dose adjustment is required for renal impairment of any severity, including severe impairment, as long as creatinine clearance exceeds 15 mL/min, so the standard 125 mg starting dose applies.

items.prompt: Ascites and elevated bilirubin meeting Child-Pugh class B (moderate) hepatic impairment before starting therapy
items.rationale: The label specifies no dose adjustment is needed for mild or moderate (Child-Pugh A or B) hepatic impairment; a reduced 75 mg starting dose is reserved for severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment only.

items.prompt: Patient starts itraconazole, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, while already established on therapy
items.rationale: Itraconazole is listed among the strong CYP3A inhibitors the label says to avoid with IBRANCE; if the combination cannot be avoided, the label calls for reducing the IBRANCE dose rather than leaving it unchanged.

items.prompt: Grade 4 neutropenia, absolute neutrophil count under 500 cells/mm3, identified at any point in a cycle
items.rationale: An ANC under 500 cells/mm3 is Grade 4 neutropenia. The label recommends dose interruption, reduction, or delay for Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia whenever it is identified, not only at scheduled Day 1 or Day 15 monitoring visits.
